title: Single-Annotation, Multi-Hypothesis Segmentation with Semantic-Spatial Residual Banks
abstract: arXiv:2610.41069v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-rater segmentation datasets show that a single image can admit several valid masks, yet most training sets expose only one annotation per image. We study single-annotation multi-hypothesis segmentation: each training image exposes one fixed mask, while the model must return a finite bank that covers held-out human annotations at test time. Our experiments reveal a representation tradeoff. Banks learned directly from images recover variations in local boundaries and extent but lose structural hypotheses, whereas frozen semantic features preserve structural grouping but underrepresent spatial variation. We introduce the Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank (SSRB), which freezes a semantic bank trained with balanced assignments and learns a residual from the image for each hypothesis. Across five medical endpoints, SSRB improves coverage of held-out masks at $K=8$ over a Probabilistic U-Net under the same one-mask constraint. On LIDC and

tldr: 提出语义-空间残差库（SSRB），在每张图像仅有一个标注的约束下，将冻结的语义库与从图像学习的残差假设相结合，显著提升了对多样人类标注掩码的覆盖率。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank (SSRB), which combines a frozen semantic bank with image-learned residual hypotheses to improve coverage of diverse held-out human masks under the single-annotation constraint.
